findings.attack: Attack 11. Planted a first-party module re-export of the json capability into an active-closure module: 'from f017_bounded_artifact_decode_v1 import json' followed by json.loads(raw). Also tested the f017_canonical_serialization_v10 source and an aliased form. Executed against a synthetic mirror tree under /private/tmp with the repository worktree untouched.
findings.observed: check_f017_bounded_artifact_decode_policy_v1.inspect_source reported zero violations and validate() returned result=PASS, violations=[], runtime_import_closure_count=32, with direct_decode_sites still listing only the two known authorized sites - the planted decoder was not even enumerated. The re-exported parser then performed genuinely unbounded decodes: raw RecursionError escaped the canonical boundary at nesting depth 100000, NaN was accepted, duplicate keys were silently collapsed, noncanonical bytes and a 5 MB string were accepted. Root cause: semantic_modules is populated only from ast.Import of json/sys/builtins, so any ast.ImportFrom whose module resolves to a first-party research module binds the real capability under a name the policy never tracks; the committed 25-mutation census re-derives json only from stdlib module names and contains no first-party re-export case. This falsifies the frozen contract clause direct_active_runtime_json_load_or_loads=PROHIBITED_OUTSIDE_CANONICAL_PARSER and is strictly easier to exploit than O-PRE-C01-003 (eval/exec/compile), which was graded BLOCKING_CANDIDATE and repaired. The defect is latent, not active: an independent name-agnostic census confirmed the committed closure contains zero such re-exports today.
findings.required_repair: In inspect_source, treat any ImportFrom that binds a name matching a capability module (json, sys, builtins, importlib, os) as a capability import regardless of the source module, and register the bound name in semantic_modules so downstream .load/.loads/.modules use is flagged. Equivalently, reject first-party re-export of capability module objects outright. Add the three accepted mutations to the committed rejection census in test_direct_parser_policy_rejects_representation_independent_bypasses, and add a name-agnostic assertion that the closure contains no .load/.loads call site outside the canonical parser and the documented offline allowance.

findings.attack: Attack 2 variant. Called AccountingRootAuthority.bind_existing with a primary root pathname that is a symlink to a directory.
findings.observed: The bind succeeded. open_directory_no_symlinks calls Path.resolve(strict=True) first, which follows the symlink, then opens components of the already-resolved path with O_NOFOLLOW, so a symlinked spelling binds to the canonical target. The consequence is benign but degraded: primary_path retains the symlink spelling, so path_status() returns IDENTITY_MISMATCH for the entire package lifetime even though the retained descriptor is correct, and no false zero is possible. Not reachable in production - _execute_installed creates the evidence root itself with mkdir(exist_ok=False) immediately before binding, and _safe_evidence_root independently rejects symlinks. The root continuity contract requires identity_preserving_handle_required and prohibits path reselection after package start, neither of which is violated.
findings.required_repair: Optional hardening: reject a primary or fallback root whose caller-supplied pathname is itself a symlink at bind time, or record the resolved canonical spelling in primary_path so path_status() does not report a permanent mismatch for a correctly bound root.

findings.observed: raw_recursion_errors, false_zero_results, unexpected_passes, original_checkpoint_shard_opens, original_checkpoint_identity_hash_reads and original_checkpoint_payload_reads are hardcoded literals in the result dictionaries, not counters accumulated from executed cases. They are nevertheless sound, because the individual case functions raise on any unexpected behaviour (for example _cross_product_cases raises when the observed package lower bound differs from the expected one), so a violation aborts the run and no artifact is produced. They are assertions-by-construction rather than measurements, which weakens their standalone evidentiary value.

findings.attack: Attack 13 variant. Banked a terminal artifact whose payload nests 3000 levels deep.
findings.observed: The write succeeded (result PASS, target BOUND_PRIMARY) because _bank_at validates only canonical serializability and byte readback, not the decode bounds. The resulting artifact exceeds max_depth=64 and is therefore permanently undecodable by the project's own bounded reader. No accounting harm follows - such an artifact observes as AUTHORITY_CORRUPT, which the monotonic rule treats as never being evidence of absence, and the journal records only the digest so the hash chain stays decodable. The asymmetry is that the banker will durably write authority bytes that its own canonical parser must reject.
findings.required_repair: Optional hardening: apply the bounded-decode limits to values on the write path in _bank_at, or round-trip the banked bytes through parse_artifact_bytes as part of the existing readback verification.

findings.attack: Required attacks 3 and 5. Planted ten mutations into an active-closure module (f017_lifecycle_artifact_v10.py) in synthetic mirrors of the 32-module import closure under /private/tmp, each reaching the real json module as an attribute of a first-party module and decoding through a member other than load/loads: parser.json.JSONDecoder().decode(raw); the canonical-serializer exporter _s.json.JSONDecoder().decode(raw); parser.json.decoder.JSONDecoder().decode(raw); a hoisted class _D = parser.json.JSONDecoder then _D().decode(raw); parser.json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode(raw)[0]; JSONDecoder(object_pairs_hook=dict).decode; a hoisted _dec = parser.json.decoder; scan_once; and functools.partial(parser.json.JSONDecoder().decode). Policy run before importing the planted runtime module in every case.
findings.observed: All ten accepted. check_f017_bounded_artifact_decode_policy_v1.validate() returned result=PASS, violations=[], runtime_import_closure_count=32, and its direct_decode_sites census still listed only the two authorized sites - the planted decoder was not enumerated. Root cause: the repair's two new helpers, _name_agnostic_decode_sites and _name_agnostic_decode_member_escapes, both filter on node.attr in {'load','loads'}, and the attribute name 'json' is absent from DYNAMIC_CAPABILITY_ATTRIBUTES, so an ast.Attribute chain rooted at a first-party module name reaches the genuine json module through a name the policy never tracks. CAPABILITY_REEXPORT_IMPORT closes only the ImportFrom spelling, not the attribute-access spelling. The planted decoders then performed genuinely unbounded decodes: raw RecursionError escaped the canonical boundary at nesting depth 100000, duplicate keys silently collapsed to {'a': 2}, NaN and Infinity were accepted, noncanonical spacing and ordering were accepted, a 5 MB string was accepted, and a non-dict top level was accepted - every one of which the canonical parser rejects as ArtifactDecodeError on the identical bytes. This falsifies the frozen contract clause direct_active_runtime_json_load_or_loads=PROHIBITED_OUTSIDE_CANONICAL_PARSER and is the same defect class as cycle-02 O-C02-001, one representation removed. The defect is latent, not active: an independent census found zero such constructs in the committed closure.
findings.required_repair: Make the gate capability-rooted rather than member-name-rooted. Track any ast.Attribute whose attr is a capability export name (json, sys, builtins, importlib, os) as binding that capability regardless of the receiver, register the resulting expression in semantic_modules, and then apply the existing json member policy to it - so parser.json.<anything> is a violation unless it is dumps in a direct call, or loads in the canonical parser or the documented offline allowance. Add the transported-JSONDecoder, transported-decoder-submodule, raw_decode, scan_once and hoisted-class forms to the committed rejection census in test_direct_parser_policy_rejects_representation_independent_bypasses, and add an assertion that the closure contains no reference to any json-module member outside the two authorized sites.

findings.attack: Required attack 4, which names operator.attrgetter explicitly. Planted three operator-module retrievals into an active-closure module in synthetic mirrors: operator.attrgetter('loads')(parser.json)(raw); operator.attrgetter('json.loads')(parser)(raw); and operator.methodcaller('loads', raw)(parser.json).
findings.observed: All three accepted with result=PASS and violations=[]. The policy rejects getattr, setattr, vars, globals, locals, eval, exec, compile, __import__, __dict__, __getattribute__ and sys.modules, and the repair added 'load'/'loads' to the getattr member check, but there is no rule for the operator module, so attrgetter and methodcaller retrieve the identical bound method with the capability name appearing only as a plain string constant the policy never inspects. Verified end-to-end: the attrgetter and methodcaller forms both collapsed duplicate keys to {'a': 2} and accepted NaN, and accepted nesting depth 100000 that the canonical parser rejects. Note that operator.itemgetter('loads')(parser.json.__dict__) IS correctly rejected, but only incidentally, by the pre-existing __dict__ rule - not by any name-agnostic reasoning about the retrieved member.
findings.required_repair: Reject any call to operator.attrgetter, operator.methodcaller or operator.itemgetter in the active closure whose argument is a non-constant, or is a constant naming a capability member (load, loads, or any dotted path containing json/sys/builtins/modules). Add all three accepted forms to the committed regression census. More durably, land the capability-rooted rewrite in O-C03-001, which removes the receiver parser.json from reach and makes the operator-module route unconstructible.

findings.attack: Required attack 5 extended to closure construction rather than closure content. Planted a package-shaped first-party module scripts/research/f017_side_pkg/__init__.py containing plain 'import json' and 'json.loads(raw)', and imported it from an active-closure module with 'import f017_side_pkg'.
findings.observed: Accepted: result=PASS, violations=[], runtime_import_closure_count=32 - the planted module is not merely unflagged, it is never parsed at all. _closure() extends only when RESEARCH / f'{module}.py' is a file, so any first-party dependency that resolves to a package directory, or to a dotted path whose first segment is not a research .py file, is silently outside the audited set while remaining fully importable at runtime. The planted module then collapsed duplicate keys, accepted NaN, and accepted nesting depth 100000. This is a total enforcement blind spot rather than a missed representation, and it is not covered by any committed regression. Latent: the committed closure contains no package-shaped research dependency today.
findings.required_repair: Extend _closure() to follow package-shaped dependencies (RESEARCH / module / '__init__.py' and submodule paths) and dotted first-party imports, and fail closed on any first-party import the closure cannot resolve to an inspected file rather than silently skipping it. Add a regression asserting that a package-shaped planted dependency raises the direct-parser policy error, mirroring the existing end-to-end mirror-tree test.

findings.attack: Planted 'import ast' plus 'ast.literal_eval(raw)' into an active-closure module in a synthetic mirror.
findings.observed: Accepted with result=PASS and violations=[]. ast.literal_eval is not the json parser, so it is arguably outside the letter of the direct_active_runtime_json_load_or_loads clause, but it is an unbounded recursive structural decoder that accepts NaN and Infinity spellings and has no depth, size or duplicate-key discipline, and it would deserialize authority-shaped bytes into the same Python structures the runtime consumes. The controlled-failure boundary asserted by C-JSON-004 would not apply to bytes decoded through it. Latent: the active closure contains zero literal_eval references.
findings.required_repair: Optional hardening: add literal_eval, and the ast module generally, to the prohibited dynamic-evaluation set alongside eval, exec and compile, so the closure has exactly one structural decoder.

findings.attack: Required attack 11, deep-artifact case. Banked a terminal artifact whose payload nests 3000 levels deep through bank_terminal_artifact.
findings.observed: The write succeeded (result PASS, target BOUND_PRIMARY) because _bank_at validates only canonical serializability and byte readback, not the decode bounds. The resulting artifact exceeds max_depth=64 and is therefore permanently undecodable by the project's own bounded reader. No accounting harm follows - such an artifact observes as AUTHORITY_CORRUPT, which the monotonic rule treats as never being evidence of absence, and I confirmed no false zero arises. This exactly reproduces cycle-02 finding O-C02-008, which was classified DEFENSE_IN_DEPTH and remains undispositioned at this head.
findings.required_repair: Optional hardening: apply the bounded-decode limits to values on the write path in _bank_at, or round-trip the banked bytes through parse_artifact_bytes as part of the existing readback verification.
